session_dialogue.text: Hello. How are you feeling today?
I'm trying to feel okay, but my head is still heavy with all the things I'm supposed to handle on my own. It's hard not to feel like I'm failing.
I can see how overwhelming that must feel. Can you tell me why you think you're supposed to handle everything by yourself?
I keep thinking about my brother and how he still depends on our parents. I don't want to be like him. I feel like if I ask for help, I'll prove I'm not capable.
That sounds really painful. Can you explain why you feel like asking for help would mean you're not capable?
Because every time I try to do things on my own, I mess up. I feel like I'm not good enough, and if I ask for help, it just confirms I'm a failure.
It’s clear how much pressure you’re under. Can you tell me why you think your mistakes mean you’re not good enough?

I keep telling myself that if I’m not perfect, I don’t deserve to be taken seriously. I feel like I have to be flawless to be seen as capable, and when I make a mistake, it’s like I’ve failed completely.
That’s a heavy burden to carry. Can you tell me why you feel like you have to be flawless to be taken seriously?
Because I’ve always been told that if I’m not perfect, I’m not worth anything. I’ve spent so long trying to prove I’m capable, and every mistake feels like a betrayal of that goal.
It sounds like you’ve been carrying a lot of expectations. Can you tell me why those expectations feel like a betrayal?

Because I thought if I failed, I’d lose everything—my independence, my self-respect, and maybe even my family’s approval. I keep trying to be perfect, but I’m not, and that feels like I’m letting them down.
That must feel like a huge weight. Can you tell me why letting them down feels so unbearable?
Because I’ve spent so much time trying to be the person I think they want me to be, and I’m afraid if I fail, they’ll see me as a disappointment. I don’t want to feel like I’m not enough for them.
It sounds like you’re carrying a lot of fear. Can you tell me why not being enough feels so unbearable to you?
Because I’ve always believed that if I’m not enough, I’m not worthy of love or support. And if I’m not worthy, I don’t deserve to be taken care of, even by my own family.
That’s a deep and painful belief to carry. Can you tell me why not being worthy of love feels so essential to you?
Because I’ve spent so long trying to earn it instead of being given it. I think if I’m not worthy, I’m not allowed to ask for help, even when I need it most.
It sounds like you’ve been working really hard to earn love. Can you tell me why earning it feels more important than being given it?
Because I’ve always believed that if I’m not strong enough on my own, I’m not deserving of support. I think if I ask for help, it means I’m weak, and if I’m weak, I’m not worthy of love.
